Show less Read more Like 44 Dislike Reply 11 replies Hide replies 11 replies @artofmkd 3 months ago 00:03:20 - Fun Fact about the artificial lakes - a lot of the lakes in North East PA were built not just for recreation but to supply fresh ice for the surrounding big cities - like New York and Philadelphia - as well as outfitting the local tourist industry. Because the winters in the Pocono's once reliably dropped below freezing every year, and the abundance of natural artesian springs feeding the streams that led to lake, the ice trade boomed from October to March until the advent of mechanical refrigeration. Show less Read more Like 5 Dislike Reply @GalpsPGH 3 months ago One neat thing about the Allegheny flowing south and the Mon flowing north is that you'll often see the Allegheny River freeze over during winter, but since the waters from the Mon are flowing in from the south, they're usually too warm to freeze. If you see chunks of ice flowing in the Mon, then you know it's been really cold for an extended period.
